financials_interim.notes: Source: BALA Interim Financial Statements, Six Months Period Ended 30 June 2026 (unaudited, board-approved 12 Aug 2026), downloaded from CSE cdn (cmt/upload_report_file/705_1786700646235.pdf). Single-entity filing (Balangoda Plantations PLC has no subsidiaries of its own) -> entered as one GROUP row per project convention for single-entity filers. First interim row for BALA in this DB (prior local doc was period ended 30 June 2025, now superseded). Figures are the SIX-MONTH cumulative column (not the standalone Q2/3-month column also shown on p.4) vs six-month comparative ended 30 June 2025, both unaudited. Income statement: p.4. Balance sheet (Statement of Financial Position, as at 30/6/2026 vs audited 31/12/2025): p.3. Cash flow statement: p.6. Segmental note (Tea vs Rubber): p.7. Mapping notes: operating_profit = 'Profit from operating activities' (242,874 vs 489,093, i.e. after other income and the biological-asset fair-value gain but before finance costs) -- this is the closest analogue to an EBIT line in this format; there is no separate 'gross profit' subtotal used operationally since biological-asset FV gains are material to plantation P&L. cost_of_sales/gross_profit fields populated from the printed lines but note gross profit is NEGATIVE this period (Rs -12.983mn) purely on the cost-of-sales/revenue mismatch at the segment level -- not itself the headline operating metric for a plantation company. finance_costs = 'Finance costs' line (-42,232); finance_income = 'Finance income' (376). trade_receivables = 'Trade and Other Receivables' (283,225); excludes 'Amounts due from Related Company' (12,092, related-party, kept out of trade_receivables to avoid double counting -- not separately fielded). short_term_borrowings mapped to 'Bank Overdraft' (174,289), the only short-term interest-bearing item disclosed; there is no separate long-term 'borrowings' line -- the company's only long-dated financing obligation disclosed is 'Lease Liability' (552,416 non-current), which is NOT included in long_term_borrowings (left null) since it is a lease liability, not a loan. capex = sum of 'Purchase of Property, Plant and Equipment' (51,017) + 'Investment in Immature Bearer Biological Assets' (20,722) = 71,739, which matches the segmental note's independently disclosed total capex of 71,739 (allocated 64,400 + unallocated 7,339) -- cross-check passed. EPS basic 2.75 = PAT 130,122 / 47,272,726 shares, matches printed EPS exactly (no diluted EPS disclosed, treated as same as basic given single class of ordinary shares plus one Golden share with no economic rights). PBT-tax-PAT identity holds (201,018 - 70,896 = 130,122). Basis of preparation: LKAS 34, unaudited. No MD&A/commentary section in this filing -- all narrative below is derived from the segmental note and the printed statements themselves, not from company-authored commentary (BALA interim reports do not include a financial review section, unlike some peers e.g. CSLK). Sign convention: cost_of_sales, finance_costs, tax_expense and capex stored as positive magnitudes (matching this DB's existing convention seen in prior ACL rows), so gross_profit = revenue - cost_of_sales (correctly negative this period) and profit_after_tax = profit_before_tax - tax_expense.

thesis.thesis_text: Balangoda Plantations PLC is a single-entity Tea and Rubber plantation company (Food, Beverage & Tobacco sector). For the six months ended 30 June 2026, Group Revenue fell 12.9% YoY to Rs.1,932,581k and PAT collapsed 65.1% to Rs.130,122k, driven almost entirely by the Tea segment (88.5% of revenue): Tea's own operating result fell 83.7% YoY as cost of sales fell only 3.3% against a 15.0% revenue decline, a genuine margin squeeze rather than a volume problem. The smaller Rubber segment's operating loss also widened despite a revenue uptick. A Rs.200,200k non-cash biological-asset fair-value gain kept the half-year profitable at all. Operating cash generation nearly disappeared (Rs.4,434k vs Rs.226,470k PY, -98%) on payables and retirement-benefit outflows, and the effective tax rate roughly doubled (15.7% to 35.3%) unexplained by any note. At ~0.61x P/B the stock screens cheap, but this is typical for CSE plantation names and does not offset the severity of the profit and cash-flow deterioration just reported (Interim Financial Statements, Segmental Note p.7).
thesis.gaps_note: Macro & Industry Outlook (10% weight) unavailable -- no tea/rubber commodity-price, Colombo-auction, or wage-board data source exists in this project; the remaining five pillars are renormalized to sum to 100% (Financial Quality 33.3%, Growth 22.2%, Valuation 22.2%, Business Quality 16.7%, Governance & Risk 5.6%). Confidence is limited: only ONE interim quarter is on file (no annual report review, no multi-period trend), no dividend/shareholder data (last three recorded periods show no DPS), and the filing itself provides no Financial Review/MD&A commentary, so the qualitative drivers (auction prices vs field/factory costs) behind the reported numbers cannot be independently confirmed.

financial_quality.rationale: H1 FY2026 (six months ended 30 June 2026) Group operating margin nearly halved YoY, from 22.0% to 12.6% (Profit from Operating Activities -50.4% to Rs.242,874k), and PAT fell 65.1% to Rs.130,122k. Net Cash from Operating Activities collapsed to just Rs.4,434k from Rs.226,470k PY (a 98% decline) on a Rs.91,690k reduction in Trade and Other Payables and Rs.62,810k of retirement benefits paid -- a materially weaker cash-conversion picture than the P&L alone suggests. The effective tax rate rose sharply from 15.7% to 35.3% (tax expense +2.5% YoY despite PBT falling 54.5%), unexplained by any note in the filing. A Rs.200,200k non-cash Gain on Changes in Fair Value of Biological Assets (+6.8% YoY) is doing real work to keep the half-year profitable -- without it the underlying decline would look considerably worse. Total liabilities/equity of 0.98x (4,538,234/4,627,987) is not excessive, but this is not primarily a balance-sheet story.

growth_outlook.rationale: Group Revenue fell 12.9% YoY (Rs.2,218,711k to Rs.1,932,581k), driven entirely by the Tea segment (88.5% of revenue), which fell 15.0% YoY while the Tea segment's own operating result collapsed 83.7% (Rs.291,670k to Rs.47,510k) as Tea cost of sales fell only 3.3% against the 15.0% revenue decline -- a severe margin squeeze, not a pure volume problem. The smaller Rubber segment's revenue actually grew 7.3% YoY but its operating LOSS widened 7.1% to Rs.(60,490)k as Rubber costs rose faster than the volume/price recovery. Both crops are moving the wrong way on unit economics this half, with no company commentary (no MD&A/Financial Review section in this filing) on Colombo tea auction prices or wage-board cost drivers to indicate whether this is cyclical or structural.

valuation.rationale: At Rs.59.70 (2026-08-28), book value of ~Rs.97.90/share (total equity Rs.4,627,987k / 47,272,726 shares) implies a P/B of ~0.61x -- cheap, though a low P/B is common across CSE plantation companies given land/bearer-biological-asset carrying conventions and is not necessarily BALA-specific. Annualising the six-month EPS of Rs.2.75 (x2 = Rs.5.50) implies a P/E of ~10.9x on a run-rate that itself reflects the 65.1% PAT decline just reported -- not a screaming bargain once the earnings trajectory is considered. No dividend has been recorded in the three most recent periods on file (FY2020-FY2022, all null), so no yield support is available in this data.

business_quality.rationale: Balangoda Plantations is a single-entity Tea/Rubber plantation company (Food, Beverage & Tobacco sector) with no subsidiaries. Tea is 88.5% of revenue and its operating result just collapsed 83.7% YoY; the smaller, loss-making Rubber segment's loss is widening despite a revenue uptick. Plantation companies in Sri Lanka also carry structural considerations (leasehold land, wage-board-driven labour costs) that are standard sector risks this project cannot independently benchmark against peers. The filing itself provides no Financial Review/MD&A section, unlike some CSE plantation/manufacturing peers, so the qualitative drivers behind the margin collapse (auction prices vs field/factory costs) cannot be confirmed from company commentary.

governance_risk.rationale: No circulars/disclosures feed exists to verify board or ownership changes. The unexplained jump in effective tax rate (15.7% to 35.3%, tax expense +2.5% YoY despite PBT falling 54.5%) with no note discussing deferred tax movements or a rate change is a genuine disclosure gap, though not itself evidence of a governance problem. No Financial Review/MD&A section is provided, thinner disclosure than some CSE plantation peers but not unusual for smaller-cap filers.

key_reasons: H1 FY2026 Group PAT fell 65.1% YoY to Rs.130,122k as the Tea segment (88.5% of revenue) saw its operating result collapse 83.7% (Rs.291,670k to Rs.47,510k) on a severe margin squeeze -- cost of sales fell only 3.3% against a 15.0% revenue decline

Net Cash from Operating Activities collapsed 98% YoY to just Rs.4,434k, driven by a payables run-down and retirement-benefit payments -- a materially weaker cash picture than the PAT decline alone suggests
Statistically cheap at ~0.61x P/B, but this is a common feature of CSE plantation companies and does not offset the severity of the profit and cash-flow deterioration reported this half
watch_factors: Effective tax rate roughly doubled YoY (15.7% to 35.3%) with no explanatory note in the filing -- a genuine disclosure gap that amplified the PBT-to-PAT decline
The Rs.200,200k non-cash biological-asset fair-value gain is cushioning the half-year result; excluding it, the underlying operating picture would look considerably worse
Rubber segment's operating loss is widening (Rs.(56,500)k to Rs.(60,490)k) even as Rubber revenue grew 7.3% YoY -- unit costs are rising faster than the volume/price recovery

horizon_notes.6m: Next interim filing (H2/Q3) will show whether the Tea segment margin squeeze persists or eases with Colombo auction prices and cost trends.
horizon_notes.1y: If the tax-rate jump and operating cash-flow weakness recur, FY2026 full-year results could look materially worse than the FY2025 base -- worth confirming once annual audited figures are on file.
horizon_notes.3y: Thesis depends on whether Tea segment unit economics recover; no company commentary yet exists in this project's data to gauge management's own view of the outlook.
horizon_notes.5y: No macro/industry data source in this project to assess a multi-year tea/rubber commodity-price or wage-board-cost cycle.

interim_updates.note_text: Balangoda Plantations PLC (BALA) reported Group Revenue of Rs.1,932.58mn for the six months ended 30 June 2026, down 12.9% YoY from Rs.2,218.71mn, driven entirely by the Tea segment: Tea revenue fell 15.0% YoY to Rs.1,709.82mn (2025: Rs.2,011.06mn), while Rubber revenue actually GREW 7.3% YoY to Rs.222.76mn (2025: Rs.207.65mn) (Segmental Information, Note 01). Profitability deteriorated far more sharply than revenue: Profit from Operating Activities fell 50.4% YoY to Rs.242.87mn (2025: Rs.489.09mn), Profit Before Taxation fell 54.5% YoY to Rs.201.02mn (2025: Rs.441.92mn), and Profit for the Period fell 65.1% YoY to Rs.130.12mn (2025: Rs.372.73mn), with Basic EPS down to Rs.2.75 from Rs.7.88. By crop, the Tea segment's own operating result collapsed 83.7% YoY to Rs.47.51mn (2025: Rs.291.67mn) as Tea Cost of Sales fell only 3.3% (Rs.1,662.31mn vs Rs.1,719.40mn) against the 15.0% revenue decline, sharply compressing Tea segment margins; the Rubber segment's operating LOSS widened 7.1% YoY to Rs.(60.49)mn (2025: Rs.(56.50)mn) as Rubber Cost of Sales rose 7.2% (Rs.283.25mn vs Rs.264.15mn) even as Rubber revenue grew, i.e. Rubber unit costs rose faster than the modest volume/price recovery. Unallocated (Head Office) items were a smaller drag: Administrative Expenses rose 4.0% YoY to Rs.80.99mn (2025: Rs.77.88mn), while the Gain on Changes in Fair Value of Biological Assets grew 6.8% YoY to Rs.200.20mn (2025: Rs.187.44mn), partially cushioning the segment-level profit collapse -- without this fair-value gain, the six-month result would have been markedly worse. Finance costs fell 13.2% YoY to Rs.42.23mn (2025: Rs.48.67mn) on lower average borrowings, a modest tailwind that did not offset the operating deterioration. Income Tax Expense was roughly flat, +2.5% YoY to Rs.70.90mn (2025: Rs.69.20mn) despite the much smaller pretax profit base, implying a sharply higher effective tax rate this period (35.3% vs 15.7% PY) -- not explained by any note in the filing, a genuine disclosure gap. Working capital moved unfavourably: Trade and Other Payables fell by Rs.91.69mn (a cash outflow) and Retirement Benefit Obligations paid were Rs.62.81mn, together pulling Net Cash from Operating Activities down to just Rs.4.43mn (2025: Rs.226.47mn), a 98% YoY collapse in operating cash generation despite the smaller PAT decline, reflecting weaker working-capital discipline rather than the P&L alone.
interim_updates.gaps_note: No QoQ comparison possible: this is BALA's first interim_updates entry in this DB with a matching financial_statements row (prior local document, period ended 30 June 2025, was superseded by this filing rather than separately entered) -- no closer prior quarter/half exists in the DB to compare against, so only YoY (vs the filing's own six-months-ended-30-June-2025 comparative column) is computed. Genuine filing-level gaps: (1) BALA's interim report contains NO Financial Review / MD&A commentary section (confirmed absent on p.1-2 and throughout) -- unlike some CSE plantation/manufacturing peers (e.g. CSLK), so every driver cited above is derived from the segmental note (p.7) and the face financial statements themselves, not company-authored commentary; (2) the effective tax rate jump from 15.7% to 35.3% YoY is not explained anywhere in the filing -- income tax expense stayed roughly flat in absolute terms (+2.5%) while pretax profit fell 54.5%, and no note discusses deferred tax movements or a change in the applicable rate; (3) no commentary on tea/rubber selling prices (Colombo tea auction average price, RSS/latex rubber prices) or wage-board cost increases is given despite these being standard drivers for CSE plantation companies -- the segment-level cost-of-sales trend is the closest available proxy and was used, but the underlying price/volume/cost split within cost of sales is not disclosed.
interim_updates.takeaway: BALA's six-month result is a Tea-segment story: Tea revenue fell 15.0% YoY but the Tea operating result collapsed 83.7% (Rs.291.67mn to Rs.47.51mn) because cost of sales barely moved, pointing to a severe margin squeeze rather than a pure volume problem -- consistent with a period of either weak Colombo tea auction prices or elevated field/factory costs (wages, fuel) that the filing does not itemise. The smaller Rubber segment is loss-making and the loss is deepening despite a revenue uptick, a secondary concern. The Rs.200.20mn non-cash biological-asset fair-value gain is doing real work to keep the half-year profitable at all -- excluding it, results would look considerably weaker. Operating cash generation near-zero (Rs.4.43mn vs Rs.226.47mn PY) despite a smaller PAT decline is worth flagging: working-capital (payables run-down, retirement benefits paid) absorbed cash faster than earnings fell, which is not visible from the P&L alone.
operational_highlights: Group Revenue Rs.1,932.58mn, -12.9% YoY (2025: Rs.2,218.71mn); Profit from Operating Activities Rs.242.87mn, -50.4% YoY; PBT Rs.201.02mn, -54.5% YoY; PAT Rs.130.12mn, -65.1% YoY; Basic EPS Rs.2.75 (2025: Rs.7.88).
Tea segment revenue -15.0% YoY to Rs.1,709.82mn; Tea segment operating result -83.7% YoY to Rs.47.51mn (2025: Rs.291.67mn) -- the dominant driver of the Group profit decline.
Rubber segment revenue +7.3% YoY to Rs.222.76mn but the segment operating LOSS widened 7.1% to Rs.(60.49)mn (2025: Rs.(56.50)mn) as Rubber cost of sales (+7.2%) outpaced the revenue gain.
Gain on Changes in Fair Value of Biological Assets +6.8% YoY to Rs.200.20mn (2025: Rs.187.44mn), a non-cash cushion that partially offset the segment-level profit collapse.

Net Cash from Operating Activities collapsed to Rs.4.43mn from Rs.226.47mn PY (-98%), driven by a Rs.91.69mn reduction in Trade and Other Payables and Rs.62.81mn of retirement benefit obligations paid.
Effective tax rate rose to 35.3% from 15.7% PY (tax expense +2.5% YoY to Rs.70.90mn despite PBT falling 54.5%) -- unexplained in the filing.
key_drivers: Tea segment operating result fell 83.7% YoY (Rs.291.67mn to Rs.47.51mn, a Rs.244.16mn decline) on Tea cost of sales falling only 3.3% against a 15.0% Tea revenue decline -- the single largest driver of the Group's profit collapse.
Rubber segment's operating loss widened 7.1% YoY to Rs.(60.49)mn as Rubber cost of sales rose 7.2% even as Rubber revenue grew 7.3% -- a secondary, smaller drag.
Effective tax rate more than doubled (15.7% to 35.3%) with no explanatory note, amplifying the PBT-to-PAT decline beyond what operating performance alone would suggest.
